answer.answer: Audit-ready reconciliation completed and persisted. The archive remains lossless audit evidence, not a second canonical snapshot; its version claim is corrected, only distinct evidence was promoted, and rejected Flowworks work remains superseded.

claims.value: The supplied `Star Rupture Game Analysis.zip` is retained losslessly: 21,674,717 bytes with SHA-256 `1a1c1ef0ae00905ced37f1221ab22c4b9268f2ebe17b7516e6c9cac67d7f6fa3`, containing 123 archive entries including directories and 115 manifest entries plus `CHECKSUMS.sha256`. `unzip -t` passed and every packaged SHA-256 passed. The original ZIP and verified extracted tree remain under Git-ignored `raw/`; tracked `MANIFEST.csv` and `CHECKSUMS.sha256` preserve auditability. The raw retention boundary intentionally contains the duplicate third-party corpus, personalized save context, generated binaries, and legacy SQLite database.

The archive’s repeated `23761620` numeric-data label is too strong. The correct two-axis boundary is: source/game-data claim Update 1, internal version `35118973`, dated 2026-04-09 and contextually mapped to Steam build `22674441`; source capture SRDB `2.3.4`, captured `2026-07-11 05:02:30 UTC`, represented by immutable snapshot `ea-u1-gv35118973__srdb-2.3.4__20260711T050230Z`; and latest public executable observed Hotfix `0.2.8`, Steam build `23761620`. The latter is not provenance for every numeric value. Imported numeric reports remain legacy calculations until ported and rerun against the canonical snapshot.

The archive’s 468 items, 191 public buildings, 234 recipe definitions, 77 Corporation levels, 121 export offers, 15 upgrades, 3,259 map markers, 3,094 loot rows, and official-news subset were semantically deduplicated against the richer RuptureOps corpus and were not installed as a competing snapshot. Selectively promoted material consists of `models/rourke-update1-save-baseline__20260711.json`; six medium-confidence Ore Excavator v2 impure/pure recipe-producer associations in `sources/recipe-producer-overrides.json`; explicit medium-confidence consumable-effect assumptions in `sources/consumable-effects.json`; nine player-specific site/geography assets; and consolidated player-save, architecture, geography, progression, exploration, food, and remote-resource notes. The comparison also corrected the building-shaped overwrite of the `airlock` item and Training Corporation’s literal `$undefined` index. Overlapping prompt dumps remain intact as provenance but create neither another game-data snapshot nor competing save versions; direct player statements were promoted once, while assistant recommendations, questions, and plans retained their separate evidence classes.

The complete 18-file `Flowworks Campaign Sizing - Levels 8 to 15` family is rejected audit history only because it over-rotated toward buffers; it must not become current guidance. The superseding staged plan reaches a level-10 cell with one Stabilizer, one Nozzle, one Impeller, two Valves, one Turbine, and two Pumps. A second Stabilizer comes later, while HRS v2 is an evidence-triggered recovery option rather than an initial build. The archive SQLite database, source snapshot JSON, core delivery CSVs, workbook, refresh script, and query script remain preserved only under `raw/`; the active RuptureOps pipeline and database remain authoritative. Flowworks is selected/planned rather than confirmed built.

answer.answer: Current-state board prepared from the July 11, 2026 save registry and planning sources. Active/installed facts are separated from proposals; a live refresh is required before making a new recommendation.

claims.value: Active sites and durable roles as of July 11, 2026: Landerworks (`LW`) is the legacy Rotor, Stator, and Applicator exporter beside the initial lander. Sunstone Station (`LW-SA`) is its active satellite, supplying raw Calcium Ore and substantial solar generation. Faraday Works (`FW`) is the active rebuilt two-Core Titanium/Wolfram/Helium electrochem Works. Brimstone Utility (`FW-BU`) is Faraday’s active critical satellite, supplying processed Calcium, Sulfur Ore, and all generation; because Faraday has no onsite generation, their rail/power path is a single important failure boundary. The First Geo Scanner fire base is a temporary defense site—not a durable production campus—but is confirmed built at the first completed scanner.
source_paths: Topics/StarRupture/Player save - sites and freight network.md

claims.value: Selected/planned, not confirmed built: Flowworks (`FLW`) is selected on a broad field between Landerworks and Faraday, with nearby Titanium and Wolfram; no Core or production placement is confirmed. Its adopted role is a one-Core-start Titanium/Wolfram mechanical Works owning Stabilizer, Nozzle, Impeller, Valve, Turbine, and Pump, importing buffered HRS, bounded Acid, Helium, Rotor, and Stator. The canonical starter is 10 machines including extractors, followed by staged Valve and Pressure Tank expansions. Grand Basin Reserve (`GBR`) is selected immediately east of GRO “Mythic Cry”; construction is not confirmed. It is reserved for separated GB-A chemistry, GB-B biotech, GB-C alloys/structures, GB-D advanced assembly, and GB-E final-product/export families. The adopted first construction is GB-A only, after preserving freight approaches, machine fields, campus plots, a combat exclusion strip, and the Geo Scanner near `3059,2618` outside the first build district. A reusable Dispatcher/Receiver Cargo service for temporary firebases and scanner assaults is also planned, not installed.

answer.answer: Little Cloud is manageable but populated; because your ammunition and consumables are valuable, bank the excess if storage is reasonably close. Otherwise advance methodically, treating the tagged Regeneration Chamber as a shorter return route—not insurance for your carried kit or a guaranteed respawn. Starry Night is easier: clear any wanderers, take the final chest first, then loot debris.

claims.value: Little Cloud is about 2/5 difficulty. Within 250 units it has 13 persistent hostile spawn entries: 8 tier-1 melee, 4 tier-1 ranged, and 1 tier-1 exploder, with no mapped Goliaths, Flingers, tier-2 enemies, or raid-class concentration. These markers represent possible persistent population, not 13 simultaneous attackers.

Protect the valuable ammunition and consumables by banking excess supplies first when returning to storage is reasonably quick. If it is not, continue methodically; use the nearby chamber as partial travel-risk mitigation and keep replacement weapons, ammunition, healing, and rebuilding supplies in a separate safe recovery cache.
source_paths: Topics/StarRupture/Player save - sites and freight network.md

claims.value: A claimed Regeneration Chamber can reduce return travel, but it does not replace lost equipment or an adequately stocked recovery cache. Historical field evidence shows that corruption disabled a contested base and its claimed chamber, causing the next respawn at the starting launcher. The exact corruption threshold and universal chamber rule remain unverified.
source_paths: Topics/StarRupture/Player save - sites and freight network.md

claims.value: Starry Night is about 1/5 difficulty with zero persistent hostile spawn markers within 250 units, although roaming enemies can still wander in. Its guaranteed final chest contains the Electronics Blueprint, Rotor Blueprint, 15 Armory Tokens, and a Frame Memory Module; clear wanderers, open that chest first, then loot debris.

answer.answer: The first Geo Scanner lesson is now preserved as operational guidance, with observed behavior, generalization limits, and ambiguous loot kept distinct. Checkpoint persisted as `checkpoint:31ae22b8-a073-aae2-b415-49938125eabd`.

claims.value: The first scanner attempt ended in death and respawn at a previously claimed nearby base. Its location helped, but it held no spare weapons or replacement materials, forcing a walk back to Landerworks. On the next attempt, the scanner fire base had installed but unpowered turrets, so they did nothing and the player was overwhelmed. Corruption then disabled the contested base and its claimed Regeneration Chamber, causing that death to respawn the player at the starting launcher rather than locally. Recovery came on the following attempt with a fully built-out, powered fire base.

The successful intervention was to build out the temporary fire base and power every turret before activating the scanner. The automated defense continuously engaged the wave—the player described hearing the turrets “sing”—and the scanner was completed, turning a frustrating encounter into a strongly positive learning experience.

The deaths, inactive unpowered turrets, corruption-disabled base and claimed Regeneration Chamber, launcher respawn, and powered-turret success are direct player-history observations from one encounter. They do not establish a universal mechanic: the exact corruption threshold and general rules governing when corruption disables a Regeneration Chamber remain unverified.

For future scanner attempts: treat first activation as a deliberate defense event; claim a nearby Regeneration Chamber but assume the local checkpoint may fail if the base loses power or becomes corrupted; power every turret and verify that each tracks or fires before activation; stage at least one replacement weapon kit, ammunition, healing, and basic rebuilding materials in a separate safe cache; do not mistake a gearless claimed base for a complete recovery point; keep the main recovery cache outside the scanner’s likely corruption/failure area; and preserve a route to a stable production base or launcher as the final fallback. The completed site appeared to yield two particularly good food-related rewards or stacks, possibly involving a quantity of 20, but the dictated report is ambiguous. The exact items and counts—and which scanner was completed—remain unresolved and must not be normalized into confident loot facts.

answer.answer: Field checkpoint: launch from the historical Faraday position and keep all exploration, progression, combat, resource, and food objectives active together. Verify the live save first because later progress and current inventory remain unknown.

claims.value: Historical launch point: Faraday, immediately north of CRRO “Warm Dawn”; Faraday was industrially ready and every then-craftable turn-in was complete. Preserve this order: (1) use the post-Rupture cave window, then Warm Dawn → Grey Owl → Lemon Souls → Purple Haze; (2) Little Cloud → Starry Night → optional scanner → Mythic Cry/Grand Basin, surveying rather than building if progression gates remain; (3) Forgotten Engine as the third focused outing—full fog clearing is not another prerequisite. Run Redleaf afterward only if the Turbine/Electromagnetic Coil blueprint package remains the actual blocker.

Keep the complete simultaneous queue active: obtain blueprints and reveal the map; collect Quartz; maintain the permanent low-chore food system; earn War Bonds for the Machine Gun; prepare for and complete the Forgotten Engine conservatively; establish Goethite and Oil supply later; and give directions using the player’s named bases and landmarks, with coordinates only as secondary precision. The food request must not disappear when conversation shifts to combat or exploration. This is a historical queue: current Engine completion, Machine Gun ownership, and later map progress remain unconfirmed.

Use a low-twitch defensive model: shotgun for close waves/corridors and an accurate rifle for Flingers, Spitters, and controlled ranged fire; exploit doors, retreats, line-of-sight breaks, and shields instead of open DPS races; carry a manual-save safety point and preserve an abort route; stage ammunition and healing before entry; and do not rely on cross-planet live ammunition delivery during combat. For scanner defenses, power and function-check every turret, stock replacement weapons, ammunition, healing, and rebuilding materials in a separate safe cache, and do not colocate every fallback with the contested fire base. Never report the recommended SLAMS-12, MAR-9, M175, LEM, or any mod as owned until the live loadout confirms it. Current location, weapon ownership, mods, Power Cell state, and blueprint inventory remain unknown.

Permanent three-item system: Nutri Block prevention (5 Prickler + 1 Oxallop → 1; stops natural calorie and hydration loss for 30 minutes; adds 45 toxicity), Calorie Chew recovery (5 Polufruit + 1 Prism Herb → 3; 40 calories each), and Aqua Chew recovery (4 Hydrobulb + 1 Prism Herb → 1; 100 hydration). Full refill: 3 Calorie Chews + 1 Aqua Chew; substitute 2 of the 64 old Hydrolites for the Aqua Chew until depleted. Depart with full meters, take 1 Block, carry 2 Blocks per planned hour + 2 overall spares, and carry one full Chew refill; double the Chew backup for a very long trip. Do not use Purfins, Antidote Gel, or another all-positive-effect remover while a Block is active; Clear Capsules are the compatible later detox option. Preserve Glowcaps as medicine: none for safe local work, 5-10 for ordinary combat exploration, and 25-40 for Forgotten Engine. Maintain Nutri Blocks at 20 minimum/40 comfortable, Calorie Chews at 30/60, and Aqua Chews at 10 after Hydrolites are depleted. Gather Prickler first, Polufruit second, convenient Oxallop next, and bank every cave Glowcap; Hydrobulb and Prism are overstocked. Evidence applies to Update 1 through Hotfix 0.2.8, assumes all Food Station recipes are unlocked, and consumable effect values remain medium-confidence until verified in game or by a first-party source.

answer.answer: The honest MVP is a manually anchored, native iPhone Watch Session built around a versioned 54-minute prediction—not an officially guaranteed game clock. It presents a five-state player timeline, makes the next meaningful event the visual hero, models opportunities as separately evidenced guidance, and uses conservative, accessible alerts whose native capabilities and limitations remain visible.

claims.value: Version boundary: Early Access Update 1 through Hotfix `0.2.8`, Steam build `23761620`, released 2026-06-17; structured source SRDB `2.3.4`, captured 2026-07-11. The 54-minute interval from local fire-wave impact to the next impact is strongly corroborated by the current tracker and an independent runtime-reading mod, but Creepy Jar has not published a numerical phase formula. It must remain a versioned community/game-data model. Use `predicted`, `expected`, `favorable`, and `lower threat`, never `exact`, `safe`, or `guaranteed`, until several Hotfix 0.2.8 cycles are validated across solo, hosted co-op, and dedicated servers. Keep game-build and source-snapshot clocks separate, exclude hidden/test content from player defaults, and downgrade confidence after a large correction, device-clock or model-version change, uncertain pause, save/reload, or server stop. Confidence states are `Unsynced`, `Manual sync - predicted`, `Confirmed at one later transition`, `Drift suspected`, and `Cycle data changed - re-sync required`; do not invent numerical accuracy before measuring it.
source_paths: Projects/RuptureOps/Rupture cycle timer - research and product design.md

claims.value: Player timeline: Fire wave `0:00-0:30`—remain sheltered; Cooling `0:30-1:30`—remain sheltered; Recovery / quiet window `1:30-11:30`—lower ambient threat, use the window; World active `11:30-51:30`—ordinary enemies and ecology active; Ruptura warning `51:30-54:00`—return, bank loot, and shelter. Anchor `0:00` when the fire wall reaches the player. The portrait hierarchy, visible without scrolling, is: sync/capability line; semantic hero state plus huge monospaced countdown and explicit target; threat instruction and action sentence; at most two opportunity cards; then exact-time next events with only `Mute one cycle` and `Re-sync` always visible. During recovery, the hero counts down to expected ordinary Vermin return; during normal ecology, it counts down to the next Ruptura or warning start. Keep a proportional whole-cycle rail for orientation, but also provide minimum-width labeled steps or a next-events list so the 30-second Fire wave and 60-second Cooling phases never collapse visually.
source_paths: Projects/RuptureOps/Rupture cycle timer - research and product design.md

claims.value: Opportunities are guidance data, not phase mechanics. Each `OpportunityWindow` carries an ID, start and end event or offset, action and caveat, evidence class and confidence, applicable game build, and applicable source snapshot. Enemy return and gathering windows remain separately versioned facts rather than universal consequences of phase boundaries. Initial evidence-backed cards cover reduced ordinary POI population, Oxallop, cave access/Quartz/Glowcaps, Ignitium, experimental Star Tears timing, Coralion/Vulpir eggs, and surface foliage/water; hide Sulheart until exact current timing is validated. Wording must preserve uncertainty—for example, `Lower ambient threat - triggered encounters may persist` and `Caves favorable now - check, not guaranteed respawn`. Surface the Ignitium/Star Tears choice because strong community evidence says Star Tears mature on unharvested cooled Ignitium. MVP personalization pins two priorities and shows at most two cards with visible provenance.
source_paths: Projects/RuptureOps/Rupture cycle timer - research and product design.md

claims.value: Alerts: enemy return and Ruptura require distinct sounds and haptic signatures, with text/symbol/border cues so neither color nor audio stands alone. Enemy-return defaults are 5 minutes, 2 minutes, 1 minute, 15 seconds, and event; pre-Ruptura defaults are optional 10 minutes, 5 minutes, warning start at 2:30, 1 minute, 30 seconds, 15 seconds, and impact. Support a player-selected exit buffer, `Full`, `Haptic only`, and `Visual only` profiles, separate phase/enemy/Ruptura/opportunity toggles, previews, and `Mute one cycle`. Never replay missed cues after resume; collapse them to the strongest current-state message. Native safety: store absolute timestamps, recompute `(now - anchor) modulo cycle duration` on resume, reschedule notifications after anchor/model/policy changes, and deduplicate by cycle number plus event ID. Disable the idle timer only while the monitor is active and restore it; never use background audio as keep-alive. A Live Activity represents only the currently armed event. AlarmKit may break through Silent mode and Focus only after the player explicitly arms the next event or session; never create endless 54-minute alarms. Earlier iOS versions use normal notifications, Time Sensitive is opt-in, and Critical Alerts are inappropriate. Show capability state and `Next alert at …`; support Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, high contrast, Differentiate Without Color, and Reduce Motion; prohibit flashing-red transitions and default per-second ticking.
